message.content:
The 200 events below are a random sample from my own Monte Carlo, not from a validated transport code (none is available here). The cross sections are approximate, so the process fractions and spectra are only approximately right.

**What was simulated**
- About 2.5 × 10⁶ source photons per run, four runs (≈10⁷ histories) through the 30 cm water cube. Each interaction whose point fell in the scoring cylinder was recorded, giving a pool of 3708 events (about 42% with unscattered 2 MeV photons). 200 were drawn uniformly without replacement.
- Compton: Klein-Nishina on free electrons, with binding neglected.
- Pair production: 2 MeV cross section ≈ 0.00035 cm²/g, from an interpolation I estimated rather than looked up.
- Photoelectric: ~0.0028 (100 keV/E)³ cm²/g, an approximation.
- Coherent: ~0.00014 (2 MeV/E)^1.2 cm²/g, with a crude angular model.
- Annihilation photons are tracked from the pair point. Positron range, bremsstrahlung and fluorescence are neglected.
- The sample contains 1 Rayleigh, 1 photoelectric and 0 pair events. The expected pair count for 200 events is about 0.6.

{
 "method": "Own Monte Carlo (no transport code available). 10^7 source photons from a point source at 100 cm SSD, directions sampled uniformly in solid angle within the 10x10 cm2 pyramid, tracked through the 30 cm water cube (vacuum outside) using exponential free paths and approximate water coefficients: Klein-Nishina Compton (free electron), approximate photoelectric (~E^-3), coherent (~E^-1.2, crude angles), pair production (interpolated). Every interaction located in the 1 cm radius, 0.2 cm thick cylinder at 10 cm depth was recorded (3708-event pool); 200 drawn uniformly without replacement. Pair energy shared uniformly; annihilation photons tracked as secondaries at the pair point. Positron range and bremsstrahlung neglected.",
